mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% over three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing corporate margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic activity and higher earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA +2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month MA by >2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage point in the same month signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise >0.5pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise >0.5pp in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in two consecutive months, accompanied by a stable unemployment rate, indicates strong labor market absorption and supports higher consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 100000 for two consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when PAYEMS > 100000 for two consecutive months and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, with no corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1), signals a savings glut that depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for four consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat (<0.2% q/q growth)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when RSAFS > 12-month MA for four consecutive months and GDPC1 is flat.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) for six consecutive months, irrespective of other macro conditions, signals a persistent weakness in the residential construction sector and a drag on GDP, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when HOUST declines for six consecutive months.
